newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem man wounded in village on Serb land - UN.
newsitem.headline: Moslem man wounded in village on Serb land - UN.

text.p: A man was wounded in a Moslem village in northeastern Bosnia on Sunday while standing in a lookout post facing a neighbouring Serb village, the U.N. said.
Adem Bejzovic of Jusici was shot in his stomach and right hand and was taken to the intensive care unit at Tuzla hospital, United Nations police spokesman Andrea Angelli said.
"The present situation is calm. There are no tensions in the village," Angelli told Reuters.

The pre-war Moslem residents of Jusici reoccupied their village in September, sparking a standoff with Serb authorities which ended after both sides signed a refugee return procedure and Serb police were allowed to conduct patrols.
The village lies in the Serb sector of the former frontline area, in a "zone of separation" between the Moslem-Croat federation and the Serb republic.
Angelli said U.N. police did not know where the shots came from, but he said the Jusici mayor had claimed the shots came from the neighbouring Serb village of Androvici.
